{{Short description|Genus of theropod dinosaur}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range =
[[Late Cretaceous]], {{fossilrange|Santonian|Santonian|[[Santonian]]}} | image = Rinconraptor Skeletal.svg | image_caption = Reconstructed skeleton | display_parents = 2 | genus = Rinconraptor | parent_authority = Méndez et al., [[2026 in archosaur paleontology|2026]] | species = pipoae | authority = Méndez et al., 2026 }} '''''Rinconraptor''''' ({{lit|[[Rincón de Los Sauces|Rincón]] thief}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[megaraptorid]] theropod dinosaur known from the [[Late Cretaceous]] ([[Santonian]] age) [[Bajo de la Carpa Formation]] of Argentina. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Rinconraptor pipoae''''', known from a partial postcranial skeleton including a partial arm and leg bone and several tail vertebrae. == Discovery and naming == The ''Rinconraptor'' fossil material was discovered during a series of successive expeditions in outcrops of the [[Bajo de la Carpa Formation]] (Cerro Overo locality) in 2014, 2015, 2019, 2023, and 2025, {{convert|50|km|mi}} southwest of [[Rincón de Los Sauces]] in [[Neuquén Province]], Argentina. The specimen is housed in the Museo Municipal "Argentino Urquiza" in Rincón de Los Sauces, where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen MAU-Pv-CO-659. It consists of the [[Anatomical terms of location#Proximal and distal|distal]] (lower) end of the left {{dinogloss|humerus}}, the [[Anatomical terms of location#Proximal and distal|proximal]] end of the right {{dinogloss|tibia}}, the isolated {{dinogloss|centra}} of ten {{dinogloss|caudal vertebrae}}, and the upper half of a {{dinogloss|chevron}}. Aside from the tibia, these remains were found scattered around the surface of a 4 m² area. In 2026, Ariel H. Méndez and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Rinconraptor pipoae'' as a new genus and species of megaraptoran dinosaur based on these fossil remains, designating MAU-Pv-CO-659 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Rinconraptor'', combines a reference to the discovery of the only known specimen near Rincón de Los Sauces with the [[Latin]] word {{lang|la|[[:wikt:raptor#Latin|raptor]]}}, meaning {{gloss|thief}}. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''pipoae'', honors Laura Pipo, a PhD student who assisted with the fieldwork that resulted in the holotype's discovery. Méndez et al. also described some additional theropod remains from other Bajo de la Carpa Formation sites as belonging to indeterminate megaraptorids. These include the upper half of an {{dinogloss|ulna}}, a manual {{dinogloss|phalanx}} (finger bone), and an [[Anatomical terms of location#Anterior and posterior|anterior]] (toward the front) {{dinogloss|dorsal vertebrae|dorsal}} and caudal vertebra. A lack of overlap with the ''Rinconraptor'' material—or the coeval ''[[Tratayenia]]'', which also cannot be compared to ''Rinconraptor''—precluded their assignment to a more specific taxon. == Description == [[File:Rinconraptor Size Comparison.svg|thumb|left|Size compared to a human]] ''Rinconraptor'' is regarded as a medium- to large-sized megaraptoran, with an estimated body length of {{convert|7|m|ft}}. [[Autapomorphies]] (unique derived features) of ''R. pipoae'' include the {{dinogloss|ectepicondyle}} being separated from the distal end of the humerus, the [[Anatomical terms of location#Medial and lateral|lateral]] (outer) margin of the tibia being straight when seen from above (proximal view), and the tibia's {{dinogloss|cnemial crest}} and [[Medial condyle of tibia|medial condyle]] having a subrectangular shape. It can further be distinguished from most other megaraptorans by having an anterodistally-oriented ridge on the humerus (a feature otherwise seen only in ''[[Megaraptor]]'') and an incisura tibialis (a notch near the [[Lateral condyle of tibia|lateral condyle]]) that forms a right angle (only seen in ''[[Fukuiraptor]]''). == Classification == [[File:Rinconraptor pipoae.png|thumb|[[Life restoration]]]] To test the affinities and relationships of ''Rinconraptor'', Méndez et al. (2026) included it in an updated version of the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of Ibiricu et al. (2025). The [[implied weighting]] tree after pruning ''[[Aoniraptor]]'' to improve resolution of the results placed ''Rinconraptor'' as the [[sister taxon]] to ''Megaraptor'', in a clade also including ''[[Murusraptor]]'' and an unnamed taxon from the [[Bajo Barreal Formation]] which they called "Clade C". Their analysis recovered megaraptorans as part of the theropod clade [[Coelurosauria]], as the sister group to the [[Tyrannosauroidea]]. }} }} }} }} }} }} }} }} }}|label1=[[Megaraptora]]}} == Paleoecology == ''Rinconraptor'' is known from the [[Bajo de la Carpa Formation]], which dates to the [[Santonian]] age of the late [[Cretaceous]] period. Its sediments represent [[fluvial]] and [[Aeolian processes|aeolian]] systems, with a semi-arid paleoenvironment. In addition to ''Rinconraptor'', several dinosaurs are known from this formation. [[Theropods]] include the fellow megaraptorid ''[[Tratayenia]]'', [[abelisauroid]]s (''[[Velocisaurus]]'', ''[[Llukalkan]]'', and ''[[Viavenator]]''), [[alvarezsaurid]]s (''[[Achillesaurus]]'' and ''[[Alvarezsaurus]]''), the [[unenlagiine]] paravian ''[[Diuqin]]'', and the [[avialan]]s (birds, in the broad sense) ''[[Neuquenornis]]'' and ''[[Patagopteryx]]''. Other dinosaurs include the [[elasmaria]]n ornithopod ''[[Mahuidacursor]]'' and diverse [[titanosauria]]n sauropods, such as ''[[Bonitasaura]]'', ''[[Inawentu]]'', ''[[Overosaurus]]'', ''[[Rinconsaurus]]'', ''[[Traukutitan]]'', and ''[[Yeneen]]''. Non-dinosaurian fauna includes indeterminate [[pterosaur]]s and fossil [[snake]]s (''[[Dinilysia]]''), [[lizard]]s (''[[Paleochelco]]''), [[turtle]]s (''[[Lomalatachelys]]''), and several [[crocodyliforms]]. == References == {{Reflist|refs= {{Cite journal |last=Méndez |first=Ariel H. |last2=Paulina-Carabajal |first2=Ariana |last3=Filippi |first3=Leonardo S. |last4=Gianechini |first4=Federico A. |last5=González-Dionis |first5=Javier |last6=Vettorazzi |first6=Lucía F. |last7=Seculi-Pereyra |first7=E.
